claims.text: Premelting and melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by self-induced copper segregation to the particle surface.
Copper has a lower melting point than the other constituents of the alloy.
Surface copper accumulation creates a liquid-like layer below the bulk melting point.
The liquid-like surface layer nucleates full-particle melting.
The initial nanoparticles are solid, single-phase FeNiCrCoCu particles with homogeneous elemental distributions.
A sub-melting anneal will enhance copper diffusion to and accumulation at the nanoparticle surface relative to an untreated particle.
The controlled comparison will examine treated and untreated nanoparticles in the 5–20 nm diameter range.
In-situ high-resolution TEM, EDS mapping, and DSC will be used across temperatures from well below to just above the nominal bulk melting point.
Heating produces faster diffusion kinetics and a thermodynamic driving force for copper surface segregation.
The copper-rich surface layer has a lower melting point and therefore undergoes premelting.
Localized surface melting facilitates inward propagation of a melting front.
Inward propagation from the premelted surface lowers the effective melting-onset temperature of the nanoparticle.
Treated nanoparticles will exhibit liquid-phase features earlier than untreated nanoparticles.
Treated nanoparticles will have a lower melting-onset temperature in DSC and TEM than untreated nanoparticles.
Untreated homogeneous nanoparticles are expected to melt at or near the bulk melting point.
The proposed mechanism applies approximately to 5–20 nm particles when no bulk phase separation occurs.
The mechanism may not apply to larger particles or to conditions producing significant bulk phase segregation.
The magnitude of melting-temperature reduction may vary with particle size, synthesis conditions, treatment protocol, and the competition between segregation and melting kinetics.
Failure to observe statistically earlier surface melting or measurable pre-melting copper enrichment in treated particles relative to controls will reject the hypothesis.
